note: A verdict and a reason for every ambiguous-ownership domain in docs/route-ownership-baseline.json's bothDivergent list: Express registers handlers for it, an edge function serves it, and nothing proxies between them, so dev and production run different code for the same path. 'unexamined' is a permitted verdict and is the point - it is what stops a guess from being written down as a finding, and this file exists because two priority-1 stories (LAUNCH-013, LEGAL-004) sat inside the flat list indistinguishable from the entries where the divergence is harmless. VERDICTS: parity (both hosts checked, same behaviour); divergent (a named behavioural difference that matters in production); resolved (was divergent, ported, with the round named); express-only-capability (Express does something the edge does not and that is a recorded gap); unexamined (nobody has compared them). Added round 124. A domain that stops being ambiguous - usually because the prefix was proxied - LEAVES this file, so the 'resolved' count is not a history of everything ever fixed; it is the domains that were ported while the divergence itself remains. Round 134 dropped catalog and enabled-products on porting them, and dropped mobile (round 113) and onboarding (round 133), whose scoped proxy entries had made them unambiguous without anyone tightening docs/route-ownership-baseline.json - a stale entry here is pre-forgiveness for whatever lands under that name next.

chatbot.reason: Round 153 read both. The six console paths (connections, connect, links, query-log) ran on an Express copy with no role check while the edge function needs a MANAGER to change an install or a mapping; they are proxied with scoped entries and the Express handlers deleted. POST /query stays Express-only on purpose - the edge function answers 501 CHATBOT_QUERY_NOT_PORTED because the tool registry needs CLAUDE_API_KEY at the edge - and its caller-supplied platformUserId could resolve to another user's scope, now refused unless the link is the caller's own.

deal-stages.reason: Round 138. One client path: LeadDeals.tsx GETs /api/deal-stages for the stage dropdown. Both hosts read deal_stages scoped to tenant_id ordered by sort_order and answer a bare array; the edge function layers sortOrder/isActive camel aliases over the snake row and Express returns the Drizzle row, and the page reads through extractRecords, so the live path is at parity. Express additionally has POST /api/deal-stages and POST /api/deal-stages/initialize (routes-workflow-mobile.ts:552, :571) with NO caller in any of the seven client trees - the edge function is GET-only. Note deal_stages is the LEGACY stage model (deals.stage_id holds a deal_stages.id; pipeline_stages.legacy_stage_id is CRMX-005's bridge), so a second write path into it is not work worth porting, and server/lib/pipeline-stage-mirror.ts already records those two endpoints as legacy creators. Nothing is broken on either host.

integrations.reason: Round 128 read all three Express files and the edge function. The phantom-`config` class this entry guessed at is NOT here: QUALITY-002's defect was on `system_integrations`, and the edge function reads `platform_integrations`, which really does have `config`. What is real: TWO of the three Express routers are mounted (routes-integrations.ts at routes-registry:386, integrations/routes.ts at :387) and the third, routes-integrations-real.ts - 320 lines, named 'real' - has no importer at all and sits in docs/server-orphans-baseline.json. MOUNT ORDER DECIDES A WINNER: routes-integrations.ts registers GET /api/integrations/:id first, so GET /api/integrations/marketplace is served by the :id handler with id='marketplace' rather than by integrations/routes.ts's marketplace catalogue - proven by mounting both in that order and issuing the request, not by reading. POST /oauth/init survives only because the shadowing handler is a GET. Nothing in client/src calls /marketplace, so the shadowing is latent. LIVE GAPS, each unserved in production: POST /integrations/oauth/init (IntegrationHub's Connect button - no edge branch, and it was a raw fetch, so it never left the static origin either), and the whole of useExternalIntegrations (GET /status and /bulk-sync resolve to the by-id branch and 404; PATCH /{provider}/config has no branch, the edge function takes POST) - though that hook's only consumer, ExternalIntegrationsDashboard.tsx, is itself an orphan, so it is COP-B03's setup rather than a live break. The /api/integrations/calendar/* half of the routes-registry.ts note is STALE: PA-052 repointed CalendarProvider at /api/meetings/calendar/*. ROUND 129 CLOSED THE OAUTH HALF, and found a security defect on the way. GET /api/integrations/:provider/callback is necessarily unauthenticated, and it took the tenant a connection is stored against from `state.split('-')[0]` - a query parameter - while never comparing the state to the one POST /oauth/init had written into req.session. Its only check, `provider !== state.split('-')[1]`, could not pass: a tenant id is a uuid, so that group is four hex characters and never a provider name, verified by running it. So the feature had never completed a connection, and the tautological check was the only thing keeping the unauthenticated write unreachable. shared/oauth-state.ts issues 32 random bytes that carry nothing, the callback verifies in constant time against the stored record and reads tenant, user and provider from THERE, the record is single use and expires in ten minutes. The edge function answers 501 OAUTH_STATE_IS_SESSION_BOUND on both halves rather than 404ing, and the page's raw fetch is apiRequest now, so production says why instead of parsing the SPA shell.

invoices.reason: Round 132. The Invoices page LISTS from /api/billing/invoices (proxied, so one host) but bulk-mutates through /api/invoices/bulk-update and /bulk-delete, which are NOT proxied - so dev runs server/routes-bulk-operations.ts and production runs supabase/functions/invoices/. Express registers only those two bulk POSTs, so GET /api/invoices, /:id, POST, PATCH and DELETE reach no dev handler at all while working in production: the split running backwards, which nobody files because production is fine. Both bulk implementations reported deletedCount: ids.length - the request, not the result - and that is fixed on both hosts through shared/bulk-result.ts, so the remaining divergence is which host serves them rather than what they answer. Converging needs either a crmProxies entry (safe only once the two bulk shapes are confirmed identical against a deploy) or Express list handlers; neither is free, so this stays divergent rather than resolved.

parts-orders.reason: Round 138. One live path: ServiceTicketAnalysis.tsx POSTs /api/parts-orders/:id/items, and COP-M01 already fixed the edge function's column map for it (part_number/part_name, part_description, quantity_ordered, unit_price, line_total - the flat part_id/description/quantity/unit_cost/total_cost names do not exist) and set tenant_id, which Express's insert does too. THE NAMED DIFFERENCE IS LATENT: GET /api/parts-orders/:id/items returns raw snake_case from the edge function and camelCase Drizzle rows from Express, so a component reading camelCase would render blank cells in production only - nothing calls that GET on either host today, so it is a trap for whoever wires the first caller rather than a live defect. PATCH /api/parts-orders/:orderId is Express-only and also uncalled. The edge function's ownedOrder() check is the half that matters and is present: parts_order_items is reached only through its parent, so an unscoped :id would let one tenant read another's line items.

quickbooks.reason: Round 126 read both. Express runs the real Intuit OAuth flow and holds the access token, refresh token and company id in req.session, under its own comment 'in a real app, save to database' - so it works on a developer machine and writes no row. The edge function read `integrations` and `quickbooks_mappings`, both phantom, DISCARDED the error on GET /status and answered connected:false at 200, so every dealer in production was told they had not connected QuickBooks whether or not they had. Both hosts also reported a sync that persists nothing: the edge branches never called Intuit ('in production, this would call the QuickBooks API') and Express called it, transformed the result and dropped it ('in a real implementation, save to database here') while answering 'Successfully synced N customers'. All sync paths on BOTH hosts now answer 501 SYNC_NOT_IMPLEMENTED from shared/quickbooks-availability.ts, and the edge status answers connected:null with CONNECTION_NOT_STORED. WHAT REMAINS IS THE CAPABILITY GAP: Express can start and complete the OAuth flow and production cannot, because the state and the tokens are session-bound - GET /quickbooks/connect has 501'd with OAUTH_STATE_IS_SESSION_BOUND since EDGE-002h for that reason. Closing it means a credential store plus moving OAuth state into a table, which is a redesign rather than a port.

rbac.reason: Round 127 read both. PROD-013's two recorded defects were already fixed - the roles branch answers {roles, pagination} off tenant-scoped enhanced_roles and permissions answers {permissions, groupedPermissions, totalCount} - so that half of this entry was stale. The live finding was larger: ROLE MANAGEMENT HAS NEVER BEEN INITIALIZABLE ON ANY HOST. GET /rbac/status gates the page on enhanced_roles holding a row, the only writer is POST /rbac/seed, and that 501'd on the edge function while dying on its first INSERT on Express - it omitted lft/rght/depth, organizational_tier and created_by (all NOT NULL, no default), wrote 'COMPANY'/'INDIVIDUAL' into role_hierarchy_level (level_1..level_8) and 'COMPANY' into organizational_tier (lowercase), and named four role codes migration 0072's catalogue does not carry. shared/rbac-seed.ts now builds the rows for both hosts, deriving every level from the catalogue and computing the nested set, and the edge seed is gated on the global roles level (gating on enhanced_roles would be circular on a tenant that has none). Also rebound: rbac_audit_log was phantom on BOTH the assign-role write (whose result was never destructured) and the audit-logs read (which discarded its error and answered [] - 'nobody has changed anyone's access' on a security screen); both use audit_logs through _shared/audit-log.ts now, ordered by `timestamp` rather than created_at. The phantom-tables baseline is one entry shorter.

task-workflows.reason: Round 138. Four routed pages (WorkflowsListPage, WorkflowBuilderPage, WorkflowDetailPage, WorkflowStepPage) drive 11 paths; supabase/functions/task-workflows/ serves ten of them and server/routes-task-workflows.ts serves all eleven. THE NAMED DIFFERENCE IS POST /parse: uploading an image/CSV/XLSX and having it parsed into a draft needs multipart plus exceljs and the Anthropic SDK, so it is deliberately Express-only and the edge function answers 501 - which is why the prefix is not proxied (an entry would take /parse from working-in-dev to 404-in-dev). Round 138 made that refusal readable: the page toasted the server's sentence wrapped in the JSON it arrived in, titled 'Parse failed' in red, so a backend that does not do this read as a broken feature; it now says 'Upload not available here' with the reason, via client/src/lib/api-error.ts. THE STATE MACHINE WAS THE REAL RISK AND IS CLOSED: the edge function carried a 40-line replica of shared/task-workflow-state.ts under a note claiming Deno could not import from shared/ (it can), while the engine imported three of ten exports and hand-inlined the rest - so three implementations of the advance/regress/completion math existed and server/tests/unit/task-workflow-state.test.ts pinned the one neither host ran. Both hosts now import and call the one module, and server/tests/unit/task-workflow-shared-state.test.ts fails if either grows its own copy. Everything else was compared and agrees: routing, the notification pair (email + user_notifications; the Node WebSocket broadcast has no prod consumer per PA-030), and the task_workflow_event_type vocabulary, whose 12 values are all in migration 0009's CREATE TYPE.
